city.name: Kyoto
city.tagline: Seventeen UNESCO sites, a thousand temples and the quiet hour before the crowds.

dayPass.label: Subway & Bus 1-Day Pass
dayPass.detail: Unlimited city buses and both subway lines for one calendar day.

hotels.name: K's House Kyoto
hotels.summary: Backpacker favourite a ten-minute walk from Kyoto Station, with a riverside terrace.

hotels.name: Piece Hostel Sanjo
hotels.summary: Design hostel with a sunlit lounge, steps from the Kamo River and Sanjo.

hotels.name: Len Kyoto Kawaramachi
hotels.summary: Hostel, café and bar on the Takase canal, with private rooms upstairs.

hotels.name: Hotel Gracery Kyoto Sanjo
hotels.summary: Efficient rooms on the Sanjo arcade, between Nishiki Market and the river.

hotels.name: Sakura Terrace The Gallery
hotels.summary: Art-filled hotel with a rooftop terrace and a large public bath behind Kyoto Station.

hotels.name: Ryokan Yachiyo
hotels.summary: Tatami rooms, garden views and a kaiseki breakfast at the gates of Nanzen-ji.

hotels.name: The Thousand Kyoto
hotels.summary: Calm, minimalist luxury directly at Kyoto Station's central exit.

attractions.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
attractions.summary: Ten thousand vermilion torii gates tunnelling up the slopes of Mount Inari.
attractions.tip: Most visitors turn back at the Yotsutsuji intersection — keep climbing for empty paths.

attractions.name: Kiyomizu-dera
attractions.summary: A wooden stage cantilevered over a forested hillside, with views across the whole city.
attractions.tip: Walk down through Sannenzaka afterwards — the slope glows at dusk.

attractions.name: Kinkaku-ji
attractions.summary: The Golden Pavilion: a gold-leaf Zen temple mirrored in Kyōko-chi pond.
attractions.tip: Be at the gate at 09:00 for a reflection without a crowd in it.

attractions.name: Ryōan-ji
attractions.summary: Fifteen rocks on raked gravel — Japan's most famous, most debated Zen garden.
attractions.tip: From any seat, one stone is always hidden. Count them.

attractions.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
attractions.summary: Towering moso bamboo creaking overhead along a path that's only quiet at dawn.

attractions.name: Tenryū-ji
attractions.summary: UNESCO Zen temple with a 14th-century pond garden that borrows the Arashiyama hills.
attractions.tip: Exit by the north gate straight into the bamboo grove.

attractions.name: Nijō Castle
attractions.summary: The shogun's palace, whose 'nightingale floors' chirp underfoot to betray intruders.
attractions.tip: Last entry is an hour before closing.

attractions.name: Ginkaku-ji
attractions.summary: The Silver Pavilion — never silvered — and its sculpted sand cone, Kogetsudai.
attractions.tip: Climb the hillside loop for the view back over the garden.

attractions.name: Philosopher's Path
attractions.summary: Two kilometres of canal-side stone path between Ginkaku-ji and Nanzen-ji.
attractions.tip: Walk it south, downhill, ending at Nanzen-ji.

attractions.name: Nanzen-ji
attractions.summary: A massive Sanmon gate and a brick Meiji aqueduct running through temple grounds.
attractions.tip: The aqueduct arches are free; the Sanmon balcony is worth its fee.

attractions.name: Gion & Hanamikoji
attractions.summary: Lantern-lit lanes of wooden machiya teahouses; maiko hurry to evening engagements.
attractions.tip: Photographing maiko on private lanes now carries fines — keep to the main street.

attractions.name: Yasaka Shrine
attractions.summary: Gion's guardian shrine, its dance stage hung with hundreds of lanterns lit at dusk.

attractions.name: Sanjūsangen-dō
attractions.summary: A 120-metre hall holding 1,001 gilded statues of Kannon in silent ranks.

attractions.name: Kyoto National Museum
attractions.summary: Pre-modern Japanese art: Buddhist sculpture, scroll painting and lacquer.

attractions.name: Kyoto Railway Museum
attractions.summary: Steam locomotives in a working roundhouse, plus shinkansen cars to climb into.

eateries.name: Inoda Coffee Honten
eateries.dish: Kyoto breakfast set & 'Arabia no Shinju' coffee
eateries.summary: Kyoto's grand old coffee house, serving breakfast since 1940.

eateries.name: % Arabica Higashiyama
eateries.dish: Kyoto latte on the Yasaka slope
eateries.summary: Tiny white-tiled espresso bar on the climb to Kiyomizu-dera.

eateries.name: % Arabica Arashiyama
eateries.summary: Riverside espresso with a view of Togetsukyo bridge.

eateries.name: Vermillion Espresso Bar
eateries.dish: Flat white & cakes before the climb
eateries.summary: Melbourne-style café a short walk from the Inari gates.

eateries.name: Menbakaichidai (Fire Ramen)
eateries.dish: Negi ramen set alight at the counter
eateries.summary: Ramen theatre: green onions doused in oil and lit in front of you.

eateries.name: Omen Ginkaku-ji
eateries.summary: Dip-it-yourself udon in a farmhouse-style dining room near the Silver Pavilion.

eateries.name: Sarasa Nishijin
eateries.summary: Café inside a converted sento, its walls still tiled in majolica.

eateries.name: Arashiyama Yoshimura
eateries.summary: Upstairs windows look straight onto Togetsukyo bridge.

eateries.name: Shigetsu (Tenryū-ji)
eateries.dish: Shojin ryori — Zen Buddhist vegetarian course
eateries.summary: Temple cuisine served on tatami inside the grounds of Tenryū-ji.

eateries.name: Musashi Sushi Kawaramachi
eateries.summary: Fast, fresh kaiten sushi at the Sanjo–Kawaramachi crossing.

eateries.name: Gyoza Chao Chao
eateries.summary: Queue-worthy gyoza bar by the Takase canal.

eateries.name: Kyoto Ramen Koji
eateries.summary: A floor of Kyoto Station given over to regional ramen styles.

eateries.name: Izuju
eateries.summary: A century-old sushi house opposite Yasaka Shrine.

eateries.name: Yudofu Sagano
eateries.summary: Tofu simmered at the table in a bamboo-fringed garden.

eateries.name: Gion Karyo
eateries.summary: Seasonal kaiseki in a Hanamikoji townhouse.

eateries.name: Kikunoi Honten
eateries.summary: Chef Yoshihiro Murata's benchmark of Kyoto haute cuisine.

markets.name: Nishiki Market
markets.crafts: Pickles, tamagoyaki, yuba and Aritsugu knives
markets.summary: 'Kyoto's kitchen': five blocks of food stalls under a stained-glass roof.

markets.name: Teramachi & Shinkyogoku Arcades
markets.crafts: Washi paper, incense, vintage kimono, tenugui
markets.summary: Covered shopping streets mixing temples, stationers and second-hand kimono.

markets.name: Sannenzaka & Ninenzaka
markets.crafts: Kiyomizu-yaki pottery, folding fans, yatsuhashi sweets
markets.summary: Stone-stepped slopes of preserved merchant houses below Kiyomizu-dera.

markets.name: Kyoto Handicraft Center
markets.summary: Seven floors of crafts with tax-free counters.

markets.name: Tō-ji Flea Market (Kōbō-san)
markets.crafts: Antique kimono, ceramics, tools — 21st of each month
markets.summary: A thousand stalls around a five-storey pagoda, one day a month.

markets.name: Kitano Tenmangū Market (Tenjin-san)
markets.crafts: Antiques and street food — 25th of each month
markets.summary: Shrine-grounds flea market held on the 25th.

activities.name: Tea Ceremony Camellia
activities.pitch: a tea ceremony in a Ninenzaka machiya
activities.summary: An unhurried matcha ceremony in a century-old townhouse, explained in English.

activities.name: Gion Corner
activities.pitch: an evening of kyo-mai dance at Gion Corner
activities.summary: Seven traditional arts in an hour: kyo-mai dance, koto and bunraku puppetry.

activities.name: Evening Pontocho & Gion Food Tour
activities.pitch: a guided Pontocho izakaya food crawl
activities.summary: Four izakaya, ten small plates and sake pairings along lantern-lit Pontocho.

activities.name: Kimono Rental (full day)
activities.pitch: a full-day kimono rental with dressing
activities.summary: Choose a seasonal kimono and obi, dressed and styled by professionals.

activities.name: Private Licensed Guide (full day)
activities.summary: A National Government Licensed Guide who knows which side gates are open.

activities.name: Gekkeikan Okura Sake Museum
activities.summary: Brewery museum in the Fushimi sake district, with a tasting to finish.
